extraction.name: MMStar: An Elite Vision-Indispensable Multi-Modal Benchmark
extraction.description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples. The benchmark addresses two primary issues in current evaluation works: (1) Visual content is unnecessary for many samples, and (2) Unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training. MMStar ensures each curated sample exhibits visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and requires advanced multi-modal capabilities.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.citeAs: Chen, L., Li, J., Dong, X., Zhang, P., Zang, Y., Chen, Z., Duan, H., Wang, J., Qiao, Y., Lin, D., & Zhao, F. (2024). Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv preprint arXiv:2403.20330.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline using eight powerful LLMs (two closed-source APIs: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro; six open-source models: LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, etc.) as inspectors. Samples that could be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs were excluded. Then, 16 leading LVLMs were used to gauge sample difficulty and split them into four levels. Finally, three experts conducted manual review to ensure visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and advanced multi-modal capability requirements. The final dataset consists of 1,500 high-quality samples spanning 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples were sourced from existing benchmarks including MMMU, MMBench, ScienceQA, AI2D, SEED, and MathVista.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated pipeline filtered samples using LLM inspectors (8 models) to exclude those answerable without visual input. Samples with hit counts >2 were excluded. Manual review ensured visual dependency and minimal data leakage. Samples were categorized into four difficulty levels based on LVLM performance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created by human experts to ensure samples meet criteria of visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and advanced multi-modal capability requirements. Two novel metrics (multi-modal gain and multi-modal leakage) were developed to assess performance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Human expert review (three experts) with automated LLM-based filtering pipeline.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human review ensured samples were visually dependent and free from data leakage. Metrics (MG and ML) were designed to measure actual multi-modal performance gains and data leakage degrees.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three human experts conducted manual review. No explicit demographic details provided.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, etc.) used for automated filtering and sample inspection.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is designed to be expanded into a larger, online test set with dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into training corpora.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark addresses critical issues in LVLM evaluation (visual dependency and data leakage) to ensure fair and reliable assessments of multi-modal capabilities, potentially guiding future research directions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark aims to minimize biases by ensuring visual dependency and minimal data leakage. However, the selection process may introduce biases based on the capabilities of the LLM inspectors used for filtering.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark may not cover all possible multi-modal capabilities or domains. The manual review process, while rigorous, may still introduce subjectivity. The dataset size (1,500 samples) may limit generalizability.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Benchmarking for LVLMs. The benchmark is designed to evaluate the true multi-modal capabilities of LVLMs by ensuring visual dependency and minimal data leakage.
